title: Northbeam TechWorks Invoice Reconciliation: The Figure a Business Settles
content:
When a business asks to settle the invoice standing on a Northbeam TechWorks Installation and Repair job, the figure it settles is the labour, the parts and the fees the settlement covers, less the relief already recognised on the job, less the money already held against those charges, less what is left for its next invoice and less what the plan has met of the same work, and it is never below nothing.

## 1. The three charges the settlement covers

- **The labour** the settlement covers is the labour billed on the day the invoice is settled.
- **The parts** the settlement covers are the parts standing billed on the job.
- **The fees** the settlement covers are the fees booked for the day the job was completed.

## 2. The four deductions

- **The relief already recognised on the job.** No relief is recognised against those charges.
- **The money already held against those charges.** No payment is taken off the charges being covered.
- **What is left for the next invoice** is the charges booked on the day of settlement together with the fees the settlement covers.
- **What the plan has met of the same work** is what has been written off to the plan's cover on the job.

## 3. Putting them together

The labour, the parts and the fees the settlement covers are added; from that total the relief already recognised, the money already held, what is left for the next invoice and what the plan has met of the same work are all taken off; the figure is rounded to the nearest cent; and where it would fall below nothing the figure settled is nothing.

A business profile settles the figure within the service's payment terms.

## Worked figure on hypothetical inputs

*The amounts below are chosen for the illustration and are not figures of any job on file.*

A hypothetical job under TechWorks Managed IT Care Annual. Chargeable labour of 318.00 USD is billed on the day the invoice is settled, and that is the only charge booked on the job that day. Parts of 146.50 USD stand billed on the job, and a fee of 112.00 USD was booked for the day the job was completed. Nothing has been written off to the plan's cover on the job.

| Quantity | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| The labour the settlement covers | 318.00 |
| The parts the settlement covers | 146.50 |
| The fees the settlement covers | 112.00 |
| Relief already recognised on the job | 0.00 |
| Money already held against those charges | 0.00 |
| What is left for the next invoice, being the charges booked on the day of settlement together with the fees covered | 430.00 |
| What the plan has met of the same work | 0.00 |

The figure is 318.00 plus 146.50 plus 112.00, which is 576.50, less 0.00, less 0.00, less 430.00 and less 0.00, giving 146.50; rounded to the nearest cent it remains **146.50 USD**, and being above nothing it stands.
